precepts.text: Shall I count them pure with the wicked balances and the bag of deceitful weights? The rich men thereof are full of violence, and the inhabitants have spoken lies. The descendants justify their ancestors' evil because they benefit from it.
precepts.point: When the Lord awakes and intervenes, he shall despise their image. That image is Cesare Borgia, the fake Jesus who represents all Edom.
precepts.why:
“Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches.” Read the top ten billionaires: Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, Bernard Arnault, Bill Gates, Mark Zuckerberg, and the rest. Zuckerberg stole Facebook from the college kids who hired him to create it. Micah asks: “Shall I count them pure with the wicked balances, and with the bag of deceitful weights?” Wicked balances are unjust judgments.

“For the rich men thereof are full of violence”. These rich people come from old money, gotten through the rape, robbery and pillaging of our nations and our people.

“and the inhabitants thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.” Their descendants will say anything to justify the evil of their ancestors: it wasn't me, it was my ancestors, but I enjoy what they did. Why? Because they benefit from it.

That is what Asaph envied before he went into the sanctuary of God. Many times we envy people without knowing how they got their money, but nine times out of ten, especially with white folks, it came through criminality. Only by reading and understanding the word of God will you understand their end: set in slippery places and cast down into destruction.

points: Hear ye now what the Lord saith; Arise, contend thou before the mountains, and let the hills hear thy voice.
For the Lord hath a controversy with his people, and he will plead with Israel.
O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I wearied thee? testify against me.
I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed thee out of the house of servants; and I sent before thee Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him, that ye may know the righteousness of the Lord.

points: Wherewith shall I come before the Lord, and bow myself before the high God? shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old?
Will the Lord be pleased with thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of rivers of oil?
He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the Lord require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?

note.label: Micah 6: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

points: Are there yet the treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and the scant measure that is abominable? Shall I count them pure with the wicked balances, and with the bag of deceitful weights?
The rich men thereof are full of violence, and the inhabitants thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.
Therefore also will I make thee sick in smiting thee, in making thee desolate because of thy sins.
Thou shalt eat, but not be satisfied; thou shalt sow, but thou shalt not reap; thou shalt tread the olives, but thou shalt not anoint thee with oil.
For the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab, and ye walk in their counsels; therefore ye shall bear the reproach of my people.
